guarantees.claim: On reset (rst_ni negedge), in_process is cleared to 0.
When not in reset and hash_process or reg_hash_stop is high, in_process is set to 1, overriding the reg_hash_done condition.
When not in reset, hash_process and reg_hash_stop are both low, and reg_hash_done is high, in_process is cleared to 0.
When none of the explicit update conditions are true, in_process retains its previous value.

assumptions.claim: External logic must eventually assert reg_hash_done to clear in_process after it was set by hash_process or reg_hash_stop, unless a new hash_process or reg_hash_stop arrives to keep it active.
assumptions.cond: When in_process is 1 and no new hash_process/reg_hash_stop
assumptions.risk: If reg_hash_done never asserts, in_process may remain stuck at 1, potentially stalling the hash engine or preventing further operations.

uncertain_points.claim: The signal reg_hash_stop sets in_process to 1, not 0, which contradicts the usual interpretation of a 'stop' signal; the intended behavior must be verified.
uncertain_points.risk: If reg_hash_stop is meant to halt processing but instead sets in_process to 1, the hash control FSM may enter an unintended state, potentially corrupting HMAC operation.
